name: AMD Instinct MI350X
memory_bandwidth_basis: '8 TB/s' per the AMD spec table, which lists 'Memory Clock 8 GHz' on an 8192-bit interface. AMD does not publish the arithmetic; treat as 'up to 8 TB/s' vendor figure. AUDIT CORRECTION: 8192-bit x 8 Gb/s per pin / 8 = 8,192 GB/s, not 8,000. The correct per-pin rate is 7.81 Gbps (8000 x 8 / 8192). (The generic 'HBM3E = 5.0 Gbps' assumption that a mechanical audit would apply gives 5,120 GB/s and is wrong for this part: MI350-series HBM3E runs at ~7.81 Gbps per pin, and AMD's own spec table lists 'Memory Clock 8 GHz'.)

flops.notes: AMD MI350X page: 'Peak Microscaling Four-bit Precision Matrix (MXFP4) Performance 9.2 PFLOPs' - no 'with Structured Sparsity' row, so DENSE. Same structure as the MXFP6 row. Note the practical consequence: on this part 4-bit MXFP4 is the SAME throughput as 6-bit MXFP6 (9.2 PFLOPs each) and the same as sparse OCP-FP8, so the argument for going below 8-bit on a MI350X is memory and accuracy, never compute.

flops.notes: AUDIT 2026-10-04: ROW ADDED, not corrected - FP64 was absent entirely. AMD's spec table prints 'Peak Double Precision (FP64) Performance 72.1 TFLOPs' and 'Peak Double Precision Matrix (FP64) Performance 72.1 TFLOPs' (vector and matrix paths identical on CDNA4). Recorded dense:true: AMD annotates sparsity only on rows it explicitly titles 'with Structured Sparsity' (FP8, FP16, BF16, INT8), and FP64 has no such row on any MI350-series page. Ratio check confirms the derivation: MI350X 72.1 and MI350P 36.0 are each exactly half MI355X's 78.6, matching the halved-XCD relationship between the parts (MI355X 8 XCDs at 2400 MHz, MI350X and MI350P 4 XCDs at 2200 MHz). This schema's precision enum has no fp64 member, hence precision 'other'.
flops.basis_detail: MI350X product page, 'Peak Double Precision (FP64) Performance 72.1 TFLOPs'. Exactly half MI355X's 78.6, matching the halved XCD count.

notes:
AUDIT 2026-10-03 (AMD's dense/sparse convention established from the MI350X page itself and applied to every row; no values changed): this page is the cleanest statement of AMD's convention anywhere in the lineup, because it prints BOTH forms side by side with explicit labels - 'Peak Half Precision Matrix (FP16) Performance 2.3 PFLOPs' (DENSE) and 'Peak Half Precision Matrix (FP16) Performance with Structured Sparsity 4.6 PFLOPs' (SPARSE) - and likewise for OCP-FP8 (4.6 / 9.2), INT8 (4.6 / 9.2) and BF16 (2.3 / 4.6). So AMD's convention is: the unlabelled-by-sparsity row is DENSE and is exactly half the 'with Structured Sparsity' row. Every dense flag on this record is correct against that rule. THE SUBTLE PART, and the one a mechanical audit gets wrong: the MXFP4 and MXFP6 rows on the same page print '9.2 PFLOPs' with NO sparsity variant at all, so 9.2 is DENSE for those formats - not sparse, and not half of anything on this sheet. A reader who assumes 'AMD's biggest printed number is always the sparse one' would wrongly halve the MXFP4 row to 4.6. The two 9.2 TFLOPS-per-PFLOP figures on this part mean different things by precision. Also relevant to any AMD-vs-NVIDIA comparison built from this part's spec page: AMD's own comparison chart here prints 'FP16/BF16 Tensor / FP16/BF16 Matrix (Sparsity) 4.5 | 4.6' and 'FP8 Tensor / OCP-FP8 Matrix (Sparsity) 9 | 9.2' for B200 SXM5 - i.e. AMD quotes NVIDIA's SPARSE numbers (4.5 and 9 PFLOPS). NVIDIA's own Blackwell datasheet footnotes exactly those as sparse, dense being 2.5 and 5. Using AMD's chart as if it were dense understates B200 by 2x. Air-cooled sibling of the MI355X. Same CDNA4 silicon, same 288 GB HBM3E, same 8 TB/s, same 8192-bit interface, same 185B transistors, same 8 XCDs / 256 CUs / 16,384 SPs / 1024 matrix cores. It differs ONLY in clock and power: 2200 MHz and 1000W (passive OAM) versus the MI355X's 2400 MHz and 1400W (passive & active).

AMD's own MI355X brochure explains the split: MI355X's higher power budget lets it 'sustain higher performance over time, minimizing throttling and maximizing throughput during prolonged or intensive workloads'. So the real difference is sustained, not burst.

Same eight-die caveat: 288 GB is one package address space across 8 XCDs, not multiple devices.

Compute ratio to MI355X is 2300/2500 = 0.92 on FP16 matrix, matching the 2200/2400 = 0.917 clock ratio exactly - consistent with the same die.

Two fp16 entries on purpose: 144.2 TFLOPS is the VECTOR path, 2300 TFLOPS is the MATRIX path. TF32 is software-emulated on CDNA4 (AMD footnote), so there is no native TF32 figure to carry over from MI300X. Sparse figures are exactly 2x dense. MXFP6/MXFP4 at 9200 PFLOPs are the headline inference datatypes and are quoted without a sparse companion.

7 scale-up Infinity Fabric links at 153 GB/s (product page; the MI355X datasheet gives the more precise 153.6) plus one 128 GB/s scale-out link. ROCm LLVM target gfx950. FP64 (AUDIT 2026-10-04, row added): 72.1 TFLOPs, vector and matrix both, dense. Recorded on the sibling nvidia-b200 comparison as AMD's 2x-B200 HPC pitch: AMD's chart plots MI350X FP64 72.1 vs B200 SXM 5's 37.
